youtube.title: Where is the wettest place on Earth? Not the rainforest ☔
youtube.description:
The Amazon giant, the island nation, or the third one? The wettest place on Earth is a hill village where nearly twelve metres of rain fall in an average year, most of it in a few summer months, because the clouds hit a wall of hills and drop everything at once. The town next door once took more rain in a single year than most cities see in a generation.
Which did you pick?

research.topic: Wettest place on Earth by average annual rainfall: Mawsynram, a village in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, north-east India, with a long-term average of about 11,871 mm a year (Guinness World Records; India Meteorological Department). Nearby Cherrapunji (Sohra), about 11,777 mm, holds the records for the most rain in a calendar month and in a twelve-month period (26,470 mm, August 1860–July 1861). The cause is orographic: summer monsoon air from the Bay of Bengal is funnelled up the Khasi Hills escarpment and releases most of its moisture between June and September. For comparison Manaus in the Amazon receives about 2,300 mm a year and London about 600 mm. Khasi villagers use the knup, a woven bamboo-and-leaf rain shield.

myths.myth: The wettest place must be in a rainforest, the Amazon or Borneo.
myths.reality: Rainforests are wet all year, but the record for average rainfall is a monsoon-hit hill village in India, with roughly five times the Amazon's total.
